detail_datum_note: Heights are measured from chart datum. A negative value predicts less water than the charted depth.
detail_shape_note: The curve between slack times is a guide. Only its zero crossings represent predicted times.
detail_lag_value: %1$d min after high water · %2$d min after low water
detail_fitted: Calculated on this device from saved observations
detail_official: Official CHS predictions downloaded for offline use
detail_derived: Estimated slack times only. No speed prediction is available for this pass.
detail_subordinate: Prediction from the reference station with subordinate offsets
detail_bound: Slack at %1$s can differ from the CHS prediction by up to %2$d minutes.
detail_gap: Slackwater has no predictions for this station.
detail_no_week: No saved predictions cover this week.
detail_no_data: No saved predictions are available for this station.
detail_copied: Your report was copied. Send it to slackwater@openwaters.io.
detail_noaa_sub: Based on tides at %1$s and published NOAA offsets, computed on this device.
detail_chs_fit: Downloaded from CHS (IWLS), then fitted and computed on this device. These are not CHS-published predictions.
detail_chs_preview: Official CHS tide predictions downloaded to this device. Heights are above LLWLT chart datum.
detail_sub_current: Slacks and maxima at the reference station are corrected by published NOAA offsets.
detail_derived_source: Slackwater estimates slack at %1$s from high and low water at %2$s. CHS does not publish current predictions for this pass.
detail_invalid_link: This station link could not be opened.
panel_swing_rank: Bigger than all but %1$d of this fortnight’s %2$d swings.
panel_max_rank: Harder than all but %1$d of this fortnight’s %2$d maxima in this direction.
panel_biggest_day: Each bar is one day’s biggest swing.
panel_max_day: Each bar is one day’s hardest %1$s.
panel_rise_def: The upper edge of the Sun comes above an unobstructed horizon.
panel_set_def: The upper edge of the Sun drops below an unobstructed horizon.
panel_noon_def: The Sun crosses the local meridian.
panel_twilight_rising: The rising Sun reaches %1$d° below the horizon.
panel_twilight_setting: The setting Sun reaches %1$d° below the horizon.
panel_edge_def: The Sun’s centre crosses %1$d° relative to the horizon.
panel_season_large: Yearly change is far larger than the daily tide.
panel_slack_compared: Slack lasts %1$d minutes around this maximum, compared with about %2$d minutes here usually.
panel_swing_explain: The difference between this swing’s high and low, %1$s.
panel_springs_follow: Springs follow the new and full moon.
panel_orbit_scale: The orbit’s shape is exaggerated to show the change in distance.
panel_season_equal: Yearly change is about the same size as the daily tide.
panel_season_river: Water at %1$s varies much more across a year than across a day. Runoff, rainfall and wind can lift or lower the entire daily tide.
panel_season_tide: The water at %1$s follows a daily tide and a yearly cycle of comparable size. The timing of a high or low stays predictable as the seasonal level changes.
panel_spring_explain: The Sun and Moon pull along the same line. Their combined effect tends to widen the tidal range.
panel_neap_explain: At quarter moon the Sun and Moon pull at right angles. The tidal range tends to narrow.
panel_perigee_explain: The Moon is near its closest point to Earth, where its tidal pull is stronger.
panel_apogee_explain: The Moon is near its farthest point from Earth, where its tidal pull is weaker.
panel_phase_explanation: The Moon lies nearly between Earth and Sun.
A growing crescent of the Moon’s sunlit half faces Earth.
The Moon has travelled a quarter of the way through its phase cycle.
More than half the visible disc is lit and the lit area is growing.
The Moon lies opposite the Sun in our sky.
More than half the visible disc is lit and the lit area is shrinking.
The Moon has travelled three quarters of the way through its phase cycle.
A narrowing crescent remains before the next new moon.
